## Introduction {.unnumbered}

This report presents key findings from the **Malawi Fifth Integrated Household
Survey (IHS5)**, conducted between April 2019 and April 2020 by the National
Statistical Office of Malawi. We explore three dimensions of the survey:

1. **Demographics** — Who was surveyed? What does the age–sex structure look like?
2. **Consumption** — How does household spending vary across regions and between
   rural and urban areas?
3. **Education** — What is the education profile of the adult population, and
   does it differ by gender?

::: {.callout-note}
## Data source
All data comes from the publicly available IHS5 microdata hosted by the
[World Bank Microdata Library](https://microdata.worldbank.org). Survey ID:
`MWI_2019_IHS-V_v06_M`.

> **Note:** The charts below use **synthetic data** that mirrors the published
> IHS5 distributions. Replace the data-generation block with
> `pd.read_parquet("data/1_prepared/<file>.parquet")` calls once you have
> downloaded the cleaned parquet files.
:::

```{python}
import os 
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
```

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: Import libraries and generate IHS5 data



# ── paths ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DATA_DIR = Path("../../data/0_raw/IHS 5 DATA sample")
OUT_DIR  = Path("../../data/1_cleaned")
OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# ── load source data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
hh     = pd.read_stata(DATA_DIR / "hh_mod_a_filt.dta", convert_categoricals=True)
roster = pd.read_stata(DATA_DIR / "HH_MOD_B.dta",      convert_categoricals=True)
edu    = pd.read_stata(DATA_DIR / "HH_MOD_C.dta",       convert_categoricals=True,
                       columns=["case_id", "PID", "hh_c08", "hh_c09"])
cons   = pd.read_stata(DATA_DIR / "ihs5_consumption_aggregate.dta",
                       convert_categoricals=True)

print("Loaded shapes:")
for name, df in [("hh", hh), ("roster", roster), ("edu", edu), ("cons", cons)]:
    print(f"  {name:8s} {df.shape}")

# ── 1. Population pyramid table ─────────────────────────────────────
roster = roster.rename(columns={"hh_b03": "sex", "hh_b05a": "age"})
roster["age_band"] = pd.cut(
    roster["age"],
    bins=list(range(0, 85, 5)) + [120],
    labels=[f"{i}-{i+4}" for i in range(0, 80, 5)] + ["80+"],
    right=False,
)
pyramid = (
    roster
    .dropna(subset=["sex", "age_band"])
    .groupby(["age_band", "sex"], observed=True)
    .size()
    .reset_index(name="count")
)
pyramid.to_parquet(OUT_DIR / "pyramid.parquet", index=False)
print("\n✓ pyramid.parquet saved")

# ── 2. Consumption by region × urban/rural ───────────────────────────
hh_cons = hh[["case_id", "region", "reside"]].merge(
    cons[["case_id", "rexpagg"]],
    on="case_id", how="inner",
)
hh_cons = hh_cons.rename(columns={
    "reside":  "urban_rural",
    "rexpagg": "pc_consumption",   # real per-capita consumption (MWK)
})
hh_cons.to_parquet(OUT_DIR / "consumption.parquet", index=False)
print("✓ consumption.parquet saved")

# ── 3. Education attainment by sex (adults 15+) ─────────────────────
roster_edu = roster[["case_id", "PID", "sex", "age"]].merge(
    edu, on=["case_id", "PID"], how="inner"
)
adults = roster_edu.loc[roster_edu["age"] >= 15].copy()
adults = adults.rename(columns={"hh_c09": "edu_level"})

# Simplify education into broad bands
edu_map = {
    "NONE":                          "None",
    "PSLC":                          "Primary",
    "JCE":                           "Junior secondary",
    "MSCE/GCSE":                     "Senior secondary",
    "NON-UNIVERSITY DIPLOMA":        "Post-secondary",
    "UNIVERSITY DIPLOMA":            "University",
    "1ST DEGREE (BSC, BA, ETC.)":    "University",
    "POST-GRADUATE DEGREE (MASTERS, PHD)": "Post-graduate",
}
adults["edu_broad"] = adults["edu_level"].astype(str).str.strip().map(edu_map).fillna("Other")

edu_sex = (
    adults
    .groupby(["edu_broad", "sex"], observed=True)
    .size()
    .reset_index(name="count")
)
# Ordered categories for nice chart ordering
edu_order = ["None", "Primary", "Junior secondary",
             "Senior secondary", "Post-secondary", "University", "Post-graduate", "Other"]
edu_sex["edu_broad"] = pd.Categorical(edu_sex["edu_broad"], categories=edu_order, ordered=True)
edu_sex = edu_sex.sort_values("edu_broad")
edu_sex.to_parquet(OUT_DIR / "edu_by_sex.parquet", index=False)
print("✓ edu_by_sex.parquet saved")

print("\n🎉  All prepared tables saved to", OUT_DIR)
```

## Demographic Structure

A population pyramid is one of the most informative single charts a
statistician can produce. It reveals the age–sex distribution at a glance
and can hint at fertility trends, migration, and mortality.

```{python}
#| label: fig-pyramid
#| fig-cap: Age–sex pyramid of IHS5 respondents
#| code-summary: Build the population pyramid

male   = pyramid.loc[pyramid["sex"] == "MALE"].copy()
female = pyramid.loc[pyramid["sex"] == "FEMALE"].copy()

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    y=male["age_band"], x=-male["count"],
    orientation="h", name="Male",
    marker_color="#3b82f6", hovertemplate="%{y}: %{customdata:,}",
    customdata=male["count"],
))
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    y=female["age_band"], x=female["count"],
    orientation="h", name="Female",
    marker_color="#ec4899", hovertemplate="%{y}: %{x:,}",
))
fig.update_layout(
    barmode="overlay",
    bargap=0.05,
    xaxis=dict(
        title="Number of individuals",
        tickvals=[-6000, -4000, -2000, 0, 2000, 4000, 6000],
        ticktext=["6k", "4k", "2k", "0", "2k", "4k", "6k"],
    ),
    yaxis_title="Age band",
    template="plotly_white",
    legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.08, x=0.5, xanchor="center"),
    height=500,
    margin=dict(l=80, r=20, t=40, b=60),
)
fig.show()
```

::: {.callout-tip}

## Household Consumption

::: {.panel-tabset}

### By region

```{python}
#| label: fig-cons-region
#| fig-cap: Per-capita consumption distribution by region
#| code-summary: Box plot of per-capita consumption by region

fig = px.box(
    hh_cons, x="region", y="pc_consumption",
    color="region",
    color_discrete_sequence=px.colors.qualitative.Set2,
    labels={"pc_consumption": "Per-capita consumption (MWK)",
            "region": "Region"},
    template="plotly_white",
    points=False,
)
fig.update_layout(showlegend=False, height=450)
fig.show()
```

### By urban / rural

```{python}
#| label: fig-cons-urban
#| fig-cap: 'Per-capita consumption: rural vs. urban, faceted by region'
#| code-summary: Violin plot of consumption by urban/rural within each region

fig = px.violin(
    hh_cons, x="urban_rural", y="pc_consumption",
    color="urban_rural", facet_col="region",
    color_discrete_map={"RURAL": "#22c55e", "URBAN": "#f97316"},
    labels={"pc_consumption": "Per-capita consumption (MWK)",
            "urban_rural": ""},
    template="plotly_white",
    box=True,
    points=False,
)
fig.update_layout(height=450, legend_title_text="")
fig.show()
```

:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## ✍️ Your interpretation
*Which region has the highest median consumption? How large is the
urban–rural gap? Are there interesting outliers? What might explain the
patterns you see?*
:::

## Education Profile

```{python}
#| label: fig-edu
#| fig-cap: Highest education attainment among adults (15+) by sex
#| code-summary: Grouped bar chart of education levels by sex

fig = px.bar(
    edu_sex, x="edu_broad", y="count", color="sex",
    barmode="group",
    color_discrete_map={"MALE": "#3b82f6", "FEMALE": "#ec4899"},
    labels={"edu_broad": "Education level", "count": "Number of adults",
            "sex": "Sex"},
    template="plotly_white",
    text_auto=True,
)
fig.update_layout(
    height=450,
    xaxis_tickangle=-30,
    legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.08, x=0.5, xanchor="center"),
)
fig.update_traces(textposition="outside", textfont_size=10)
fig.show()
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## ✍️ Your interpretation
*Where is the biggest gender gap? At which level do we see drop-off
for both sexes? Does this match your expectations for a low-income
Southern African country?*
:::
